feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. There is no earlier race data yet, so the only evidence is the public contract and the candidate's own contents. The geometry is valid: five sensors at x = +0.04 to -0.04 and y = 0.03 are within limits, the sensor_size of 0.012 is allowed, and the wheel_track, wheel_radius, mass and body dimensions all sit inside their ranges. The weights [2, 1, 0, -1, -2] match the sign convention, with positive x on the left. The controller is in range: kp = 2, ki = 0, kd = 0.05, base_speed = 1.6, and line_loss = last_direction. Two risks to check once telemetry arrives. First, the contract allows the signal to reach about ±2, so kp = 2 can produce a turn of about ±4, which is roughly ±1400 PWM across the wheels. That may be aggressive on the slalom and could show up as high steering_oscillation. Second, base_speed = 1.6 gives PWM about 3276, and the course needs an average of roughly 1.5 m/s to finish inside 3 s. Completion time will tell us whether that margin holds, but line loss on tight bends may cap the speed. Next-race guidance: if steering_oscillation is high or max_error is large on the slalom, reduce kp to about 1.2 to 1.5 and keep kd at 0.05 to 0.1. If line_loss_events is nonzero, lower base_speed to about 1.3 to 1.4 or change line_loss to search_right. If completed is 1 but completion_time is above about 2.8 s with low error, raise base_speed to about 1.8. This is the first iteration with no baseline to compare against, so the candidate is valid and not obviously broken. Racing it gives more useful telemetry than another revision round.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation is high or max_error is large on the slalom (the contract allows signal up to ±2, so kp = 2 gives turn up to ±4), reduce kp to about 1.2 to 1.5 and set kd to 0.05 to 0.1.
